faculty: Pusat Pakar Klinikal dan Penyelidikan Kanser (PPKPK)
programme_overview: The Master of Medicine (Nuclear Medicine) is a four-year postgraduate clinical programme designed to produce competent and well-versed nuclear medicine specialists. The programme trains medical graduates in diagnostic and therapeutic nuclear medicine, radiopharmaceutical handling, medical physics, dosimetry, radiation protection, and research methodologies. Graduates are equipped to face the challenges of modern nuclear medicine practice through structured clinical training and research exposure.
unique_features: The only Master of Medicine (Nuclear Medicine) programme offered in Malaysia
First cohort of nuclear medicine physicians graduated in 2012
More than 37 nuclear medicine physicians produced and serving hospitals nationwide
Strong multidisciplinary clinical, academic and research ecosystem
Use of advanced imaging technologies such as SPECT-CT
learning_methods: Clinical training in accredited nuclear medicine centres

programme_educational_objectives.description: Graduates advocate clinical competency in nuclear medicine skills and knowledge through evidence-based medicine as nuclear medicine physicians.
Graduates embrace lifelong learning and self-development through creativity and technological innovation in nuclear medicine.
Graduates demonstrate the ability to develop, lead, and sustain a conducive working and training environment.
Graduates demonstrate competency to conduct clinical research adhering to ethics and professionalism.

programme_learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate a comprehensive and systematic approach to solving complex healthcare issues related to nuclear medicine using evidence-based medical knowledge.
Contribute substantially to the area of specialisation through originality and independent research that meets international standards.
Competently perform diagnostic and therapeutic nuclear medicine procedures independently with high accuracy.
Work collaboratively and ethically with patients, peers, healthcare teams and the wider community.
Communicate effectively in clinical, academic and professional nuclear medicine settings.
Use appropriate digital technologies and software to enhance study, research and clinical practice.
Integrate quantitative analysis to support evidence-based patient care and research.
Demonstrate leadership, autonomy and responsibility in clinical planning, resource management and problem-solving.
Incorporate independent lifelong learning and self-development to enhance professional growth.
Demonstrate an entrepreneurial mindset in advancing nuclear medicine practice.
Demonstrate ethical conduct, professionalism and adherence to regulatory standards in patient care and research.

focus: Basic clinical imaging (nuclear medicine and radiology)
Applied medical physics and nuclear pharmacy

admission_requirements: MBBS or MD with at least 2 years of clinical experience
Registered with the Malaysian Medical Council
Foreign applicants must complete 3–6 months of clinical attachment in Malaysia
